audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's direct complaint to God: bitterness of soul, objection to condemnation without explanation, creation/body imagery, hidden divine purpose, and plea for a little relief before death-shadow.

verses.restored: My soul loathes my life; I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

familiar.text: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.restored: I will say to the Divine, Do not declare me wicked; make me know why you contend with me.

familiar.text: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

verses.restored: Is it good for you to oppress, to reject the labor of your hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

familiar.text: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

verses.restored: Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?

familiar.text: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

verses.restored: Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like the days of a strong man,

familiar.text: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man’s days,

verses.restored: that you seek out my guilt and search for my sin,

familiar.text: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?

verses.restored: though you know that I am not wicked, and there is no one who can rescue from your hand?

familiar.text: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.

verses.restored: Your hands shaped me and made me, together all around; yet you would swallow me up.

familiar.text: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

verses.restored: Remember, please, that you made me like clay; will you return me to dust?

familiar.text: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

verses.restored: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

familiar.text: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

verses.restored: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and wove me with bones and sinews.

familiar.text: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.

verses.restored: Life and covenant-kindness you gave me, and your visitation guarded my spirit.

familiar.text: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

verses.restored: Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was with you.

familiar.text: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.

verses.restored: If I sinned, you would watch me, and you would not acquit me from my guilt.

familiar.text: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

verses.restored: If I am wicked, woe to me; and if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head, filled with shame and seeing my affliction.

familiar.text: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

verses.restored: If my head rises, you hunt me like a lion and again show yourself wonderful against me.

familiar.text: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.

verses.restored: You renew your witnesses against me and increase your vexation with me; changes and an army are with me.

familiar.text: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.

verses.restored: Why then did you bring me out from the womb? I would have expired, and no eye would have seen me.

familiar.text: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!

verses.restored: I would have been as though I had not been, carried from womb to grave.

familiar.text: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

verses.restored: Are not my days few? Stop, turn from me, so I may brighten a little,

familiar.text: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

verses.restored: before I go and do not return, to the land of darkness and deep shadow,

familiar.text: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

verses.restored: a land of gloom like thick darkness, of deep shadow without order, where light is like thick darkness.

familiar.text: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.
